title: CVE-2026-13149 in brace-expansion 1.1.15 / 2.1.1 (ReDoS-style exponential expansion DoS)
description: The `brace-expansion` package resolved transitively into the repository's `pnpm-lock.yaml` at two vulnerable installations — `1.1.15` and `2.1.1` — is affected by **CVE-2026-13149**. The `expand()` function exhibits exponential-time complexity when processing a crafted string containing many consecutive non-expanding `{}` brace groups, allowing an attacker-controlled input to block the Node.js event loop.
impact: If a code path in the build/CLI tooling (Metro bundler's `minimatch`/`glob` usage during Expo/React Native builds) ever passes attacker-influenced glob patterns to `brace-expansion.expand()`, an attacker could trigger CPU exhaustion and stall the bundler/build process (denial of service of the build pipeline). No confidentiality or integrity impact is associated with this CVE.
technical_analysis: Two separate resolutions exist in the lockfile: `brace-expansion@1.1.15` is pulled in via `mobile/package.json`'s `react-native@0.81.5 > glob@7.2.3 > minimatch@3.1.5`, and `brace-expansion@2.1.1` is pulled in via `expo@54.0.36 > @expo/cli@54.0.26 > minimatch@9.0.9`. Both are deep transitive dependencies of the Metro bundler / Expo CLI toolchain used only at build/dev time for the mobile app, not imported by any application source under `src/`, `mobile/app`, or `packages/core`.
remediation_steps: Bump the mobile workspace's `react-native` and `expo` dependencies to versions that resolve a patched `minimatch`/`glob`/`brace-expansion` chain, or force the resolution directly with a pnpm `pnpm.overrides` entry pinning `brace-expansion` to `>=1.1.16 <2.0.0 || >=2.1.2` in the root `package.json`. Re-run `pnpm install` and confirm the lockfile no longer resolves the vulnerable versions.
evidence:
**Advisory evidence:** `CVE-2026-13149` applies to `brace-expansion` at installed version `1.1.15 (also present as 2.1.1)`. The advisory is fixed in `1.1.16, 2.1.2, 5.0.7`.

**Transitive dependency:** introduced by the direct dependency `react-native@0.81.5`.

**Dependency chain:** `react-native@0.81.5 > glob@7.2.3 > minimatch@3.1.5 > brace-expansion@1.1.15`

**Usage analysis:** not imported by application code. `rg` search across `src/`, `mobile/app`, `mobile/components`, `packages/core`, and `supabase` for `brace-expansion` imports returned no matches; the package is only reachable via the Metro/Expo CLI dependency chain (`react-native@0.81.5 > glob@7.2.3 > minimatch@3.1.5 > brace-expansion` and `expo@54.0.36 > @expo/cli@54.0.26 > minimatch@9.0.9 > brace-expansion`). This is a prioritization signal from static analysis, not a proof of exploitability or of safety.
assumptions: This package is only reachable through the Metro/Expo CLI build toolchain used to build and test the mobile app locally; it is not imported by any application runtime code, so exploitation would require an attacker to control build-time inputs (e.g. a malicious glob pattern in a CI/build configuration), which is a low-likelihood scenario in this codebase's normal usage.

title: CVE-2026-14257 in brace-expansion 1.1.15 / 2.1.1 (memory-exhaustion DoS)
description: The transitively-resolved `brace-expansion` installations (`1.1.15` and `2.1.1`) in the repository's `pnpm-lock.yaml` are affected by **CVE-2026-14257**. The `expand()` function bounds the result *count* via a `max` option but not the *length* of each result string, so chaining multiple brace groups lets an attacker keep the count under the limit while making each result progressively longer, causing memory exhaustion.
impact: A crafted glob/brace pattern reaching `expand()` in the Metro/Expo CLI build toolchain could exhaust available memory and crash or hang the build process. No confidentiality or integrity impact is associated with this CVE.
technical_analysis: Same dual-resolution situation as CVE-2026-13149: `1.1.15` via `react-native@0.81.5 > glob@7.2.3 > minimatch@3.1.5`, and `2.1.1` via `expo@54.0.36 > @expo/cli@54.0.26 > minimatch@9.0.9`. Both are deep build-tool transitive dependencies, not imported by application source.

title: CVE-2025-71329 in image-size 1.2.1 (infinite loop via zero-size box in JXL/HEIF parser)
description: The `image-size` package resolved to `1.2.1` in the repository's `pnpm-lock.yaml` is affected by **CVE-2025-71329**. Supplying a crafted image buffer with a zero-valued size field in a recognized box-type can trigger an infinite loop in the JXL or HEIF image parsers, permanently blocking the Node.js event loop.
impact: If Metro (React Native's bundler) uses `image-size` to probe dimensions of an attacker-supplied image asset during a build or asset-serving step, a crafted JXL/HEIF file could hang the Node.js process indefinitely. No published fix is currently available; there is no confidentiality or integrity impact associated with this CVE.
technical_analysis: `image-size@1.2.1` is a deep transitive dependency of Metro (the React Native bundler), reached via `react-native@0.81.5 > @react-native/community-cli-plugin@0.81.5 > metro@0.83.3`. It is used internally by Metro's asset pipeline to read image dimensions during bundling/dev-server operation; the application code in `mobile/` never imports it directly.
remediation_steps: No fixed version has been published upstream as of this scan. Track the `image-size` GitHub repository for a patched release and upgrade Metro/`react-native` once available. In the interim, avoid running Metro's dev server or bundler against untrusted image assets, and consider a pnpm `pnpm.overrides` pin once a fix ships.

title: CVE-2026-59869 in js-yaml 3.14.2 / 4.2.0 (quadratic CPU via merge-key chains)
description: The `js-yaml` package resolved to both `3.14.2` and `4.2.0` in the repository's `pnpm-lock.yaml` is affected by **CVE-2026-59869**. Parsing a document whose size grows only linearly but contains a chain of mappings using merge keys (each merging the previous one) causes `js-yaml` to spend quadratic CPU time, enabling a denial-of-service via a crafted YAML document.
impact: If build tooling ever parses an attacker-influenced YAML document with this `js-yaml` instance, CPU exhaustion could stall the build/test process. No confidentiality or integrity impact is associated with this CVE.
technical_analysis: Two resolutions exist: `js-yaml@3.14.2` via the Jest/Babel coverage-config chain (`react-native@0.81.5 > babel-jest@29.7.0 > babel-plugin-istanbul@6.1.1 > @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config@1.1.0`), and `js-yaml@4.2.0` via the Expo CLI (`expo@54.0.36 > @expo/cli@54.0.26 > @expo/xcpretty@4.4.4`). Both are build/test-tooling transitive dependencies, not imported by application source.
remediation_steps: Upgrade `jest`/`babel-jest`/`react-native` and `expo`/`@expo/cli` to versions that resolve a patched `js-yaml` (`3.15.0`/`4.3.0` or later), or add a pnpm `pnpm.overrides` entry pinning `js-yaml` in the root `package.json`, then regenerate the lockfile.
evidence:

**Dependency chain:** `react-native@0.81.5 > babel-jest@29.7.0 > babel-plugin-istanbul@6.1.1 > @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config@1.1.0 > js-yaml@3.14.2`

title: CVE-2026-53550 in js-yaml 3.14.2 (quadratic CPU via repeated merge-key aliases)
